content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product obtained from the whole rice kernel after only the outer husk is removed. Brown rice flour is milled from the whole grain, retaining the bran and germ, which makes it more nutritious than refined white rice flour.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains more B‑vitamins, magnesium, and fiber compared with white rice.
Brown rice flour is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
In Japan and China, brown rice is traditionally used in dishes that require a firmer texture, such as rice cakes and flatbreads.
Whole brown rice contains oils in the germ that can oxidize, so it is best stored in the refrigerator or in airtight packaging.
Brown rice flour is a common ingredient in gluten‑free baking mixes, improving crumb structure and adding a nutty aroma.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function and participates in energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B3, and B6 are important for carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Brown rice has a lower GI than white rice, helping to avoid rapid spikes in blood glucose after meals.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Brown rice can accumulate trace amounts of arsenic from soil; it is advisable to rotate it with other grains.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small percentage of people may experience allergic reactions to rice or its derivatives.

items.title: Shelf‑life
items.content: Because of the oil in the germ, whole brown rice and its flour can become rancid if stored at room temperature for long periods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Brown rice flour is used in gluten‑free baking, breading, sauces, and soups. Cook brown rice with a water‑to‑rice ratio of about 2.5:1, adding salt and spices. It works well in salads, pilafs, risottos, or as a side dish for vegetables and meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For storage longer than six months, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer. Keep brown rice flour sealed and refrigerated to prevent oil oxidation.
